predecessors.name: Holy Roman Empire
predecessors.text: the Welf lands that Otto the Child exchanged for the duchy: 'In 1235, Otto I was enfeoffed with the newly founded Duchy of Brunswick-Lüneburg at the Court of Mainz'

successors.name: Electorate of Hanover
successors.text: Calenberg-Göttingen, Grubenhagen, Hoya and Diepholz in 1692, 'The old Principality of Calenberg thus adopted the new name of Electorate of Hanover'; the Principality of Lüneburg in 1705

successors.name: Kingdom of Westphalia
successors.text: the Wolfenbüttel principality, 'held as part of the Kingdom of Westphalia' 1807-1813

ledger.x: 13 May 1523: the Quedlinburg Recess ends the feud, the 'last medieval feud'; field peace had been made on 15 October 1521.
13 May 1523: the Welfs take the Great Stift.
1582: Hoya. 'In 1582 when the counts of Hoya died out, the larger part of the county went to Calenberg.'

1692: the Calenberg line is made elector ('Ernest Augustus acquired the right to be a prince-elector as the Prince-Elector of Brunswick-Lüneburg'); 'The old Principality of Calenberg thus adopted the new name of Electorate of Hanover'.
1692: Calenberg and the lands joined to it become the Electorate of Hanover.
1807: the Wolfenbüttel line loses its independence.

wars.name: War of the Lüneburg Succession
wars.outcome: The Peace of Hanover (1373) ended it 'at least for the time being'; the Welf Henry won at Winsen an der Aller on 28 May 1388 and the 1389 inheritance treaty 'finally secured' the principality for the Welfs.

wars.name: Hildesheim Diocesan Feud
wars.outcome: Hildesheim won the Battle of Soltau (28 June 1519, about 3,500 Welf dead, Eric of Calenberg captured) but lost politically; the Quedlinburg Recess of 13 May 1523 gave the Great Stift to Wolfenbüttel and Calenberg; the Main Treaty of Hildesheim returned most…

certainty.note: The pages give principalities, towns and Ämter, not boundaries; the only dated frontier changes are the 1523 Recess and the 1643 treaty.
